committed_before_any_measurement: These limits are in the commit before the first comparison or training run through cumlx.sim. A smoke run that opened each engine came first: it compared nothing, and it trained nothing.
scope: The tasks are in the style of Isaac Lab's direct tasks. They are not Isaac Lab, its assets or PhysX. These limits do not change a gate of M4.

trajectory.question: Do Genesis and MuJoCo agree from the same start under the same actions?
trajectory.measure: For each world, the largest absolute difference over all steps and values, in meters and radians. Median and p90 over worlds. The largest world is reported, and is not limited.

go2_flat.why_wider: Each engine has its own contact model, and the robot lands on its feet in this window.

cartpole_before_rail.written: After the cartpole test above failed, and before any run on these seeds. It asks another question, and the test above stays failed.
cartpole_before_rail.why: The first failure's data show agreement to about 1e-6 until the carts reach the end of the rail, at about 50 control steps. So this asks how close the two engines are with no joint limit active. It says nothing about joint limits, where the engines differ.

trajectory.control: MuJoCo with a 4 times smaller time step against MuJoCo, reported beside each task, to show the size of the time step's own effect.

cartpole.pass: upright fraction of the last 100 control steps at least 0.95 with the trained policy in MLX. First iteration and no-action controls at most 0.20.

go2_flat.pass: With a fixed command, mean forward speed within 0.2 m/s of +0.8 and -0.8, within 0.1 m/s of 0 for the stop command, and both controls within 0.1 m/s of 0. Falls at most 0.1 per world in 1000 steps.

policy_in_mlx.reference: rsl_rl's own actor, on observations of the closed loop

absolute_rule.written: After the first rule failed on the trained cartpole policy on MuJoCo, seed 7: worst rel_l2 1.30e-4 against 1e-4, on 2 of 8 batches. That failure stays in the record. This rule was written before any run of it, and before the Genesis runs.
absolute_rule.why: The absolute error stays at 3e-7 to 1e-6 on all batches. The relative error grows only when the pole is balanced and the action is near 8e-4. On those batches torch in float32 is itself 8e-5 from torch in float64, so the first rule's limit is close to the rounding of float32.
absolute_rule.unit: Largest absolute difference of one action value. An action of 1 is 20 N on cartpole, and 0.25 rad on Go2.

camera.written: Before the first camera frame through cumlx.sim.
camera.question: Does a camera on a cumlx.sim task show the physics state of each link?
camera.protocol: examples/physics-camera/sim_camera.py: cartpole, one world, 21 frames over 1 second, on Genesis on Metal and on MuJoCo. RGB, depth and segmentation from Mitsuba on Metal.
camera.limits: PIXEL_LIMIT 3 px and the floor limits in cumlx.render.sensors, unchanged from M5
camera.pass: All frames pass for the right scenario, and at least one frame fails for each wrong case
wrong_cases_that_must_fail: the renderer keeps the first pose
the renderer's camera is 0.3 m away from the camera that the check uses

camera_surface.written: After the camera test above failed, and before any run of this rule, with a new start seed. The test above stays failed: on MuJoCo, seed 7, the pole's centroid is 2.3 to 5.1 px from its projection in 20 of 21 frames, limit 3 px. The cart stays within 0.35 px, and it hides the base of the pole, which moves the pole's centroid.
camera_surface.question: Does each pixel of a link lie on the box at its physics pose?
camera_surface.measure: Each pixel of a link goes back to 3D with the check camera and the depth. The distance outside the box at the physics pose, p99 over the link's pixels.
camera_surface.floor: The floor limits in cumlx.render.sensors, unchanged from M5
camera_surface.pass: All frames pass for the right scenario on both engines, and at least one frame fails for each wrong case

first_run_failed_on_a_bug_of_the_task: The first comparison, on 2026-11-04, ran with cartpole's action driving both the slider and the hinge, so a torque of up to 20 N m spun the pole. It failed these limits, and so did the time step control. The raw summary stays in validation/m4-sim.json. The fix is `actuated` in the task. The limits above did not change.
memory: Each run goes through spikes/run_guarded.py: stop at 38 GB in use, start at 33 GB or less, 16 GB per process group.
